title: About Access Policies for Global Rules

blocks.text: This feature is in limited availability. To learn more, contact Zscaler Support.

You can implement role-based access control using access policy rules. To configure an access policy, you must first define the global rules and policy groups. To configure a global rule, you must first define the users and then define which applications they can access. For a complete list of ranges and limitations for global rules, see Ranges & Limitations.
Global rules provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Apply organization-wide access policies consistently across all applications without duplicating rules.
Simplify policy management by defining common rules once and automatically applying them throughout your environment.
Improve policy consistency and reduce configuration errors by centralizing shared access controls.
Reduce administrative overhead by eliminating the need to maintain the same rules across multiple policy groups.

blocks.text: Private Access (ZPA) evaluates access policy rules using the most specific application segment and a top-down, first-match principle. To learn more, see Policy Evaluation Order.
Before you enable global rules, review the following prerequisites and migration considerations:

blocks.item: Ensure that Application Scaling is enabled and that all of its specific prerequisites are fully met. To learn more, see Using Application Scaling.
Have Zscaler Experience Center enabled. To learn more, see What Is Zscaler Experience Center?
Global rules are only supported for Experience Center.

Ensure that legacy cloud service API automation and workflows for access policies are updated. The legacy Private Access cloud service API calls are not supported for managing policies after global rules and policy groups are enabled. To learn more, see Configuring Policy Groups Using API, Configuring Policy Group Rules Using API, and Configuring Access Policies Using API.

blocks.text: On the Global Rules page (Private Access > Policy > Access Policy > Global Rules), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View the page by policy groups or rules.
Add a new global rule.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Show or hide the filters on the page.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied.
View a list of configured global rules. For each rule, you can see:

Rule Order: The policy evaluation order number for the rule. Private Access applies policy rules based on the order they are listed here. Change the rule order by clicking the number and manually entering a new value.

Updating the rule order of an access policy configured using Zscaler Deception is not supported. When changing the rule order of a regular access policy and there is an access policy configured using Deception, the rule order of the regular access policy must be greater than the rule order for an access policy configured using Deception.
Click the rule to open a drawer showing its criteria.
Rule Name: The name of the rule.
Status: The status of the rule (i.e., Enabled or Disabled).
Rule Action: Indicates the action for the rule (i.e., Allow Access, Block Access, or Require Approval).
Bulk move or delete global rules.
Edit a global rule.
Delete a global rule.
Move or copy the global rule.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
Go to the Policy Groups page to view all configured policy groups.
